newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end higher on late stop-loss buying.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end higher on late stop-loss buying.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures settled higher on Tuesday on stop-loss buying, following a weaker-than-expected official forecast for a recovery in machinery orders in the April-June period.

The Economic Planning Agency said on Tuesday that it expected private machinery orders to rise 4.5 percent in the April-June quarter from the previous quarter, after falling 7.0 percent in the January-March period.
The forecast rise in machinery orders in the April-June period of 4.5 percent was at the lower end of market expectations of between plus five and 10 percent, traders said.
"Late stop-loss buying suggested that some people had expected a stronger recovery in the April-June period (despite the rise in sales tax from April 1)," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank.

Traders said the recent selling was based on a view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may raise interest rates if a negative impact from the sales tax rise is not as serious as expected. But there has so far been no solid data to check the view.
"Those who sold in panic (last week) were covering their short positions. But such buying would not be powerful enough to lift the December above 99.00," said a city bank dealer.
Traders said the December contract is likely to move in a range between a recent low of 98.82 hit on Friday and 99.00 in the near future.
"Operators now think even if the BOJ raises interest rates, it would be after its quarterly 'tankan' corporate survey (to be released in early July)," said a trust bank dealer.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, rates fell across the yield curve given falls in yen bond yields, traders said.
The five-year IRS rate was quoted at 2.12/2.16 percent as of 0740 GMT, down from Monday's 2.18/2.22 percent.
The 10-year IRS rate was quoted at 2.95/2.99 percent, down from 3.04/08 percent on Monday.
The BOJ continued a neutral credit stance for a second day in the morning by refraining from conducting an operation.
The key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.47 percent, unchanged from Monday's level.
Traders said banks' fund-raising demand has stabilised ahead of the end of the current bank reserves reporting period on Thursday.

About 10 billion yen of two-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.55 percent, unchanged from Monday's issued rate. But neither the benchmark three-month CD nor the one-month CD was issued.
